description: The pie chart illustrates the distribution of media sources cited in the analysis of narrative media framing within political discourse, with each slice representing a different news outlet and its corresponding frequency of citation. The chart is divided into 14 distinct segments, each labeled with the name of a media organization and a numerical value indicating its count. The largest segment, colored dark blue, represents Breitbart with a value of 14, followed by The Daily Caller and Drudge Report, both with a value of 8. The Huffington Post is represented by a green segment with a value of 7. Other notable segments include The Guardian (5), NPR (6), and Vox (6), all in distinct colors. Smaller segments include BBC (5), RT (4), Daily Kos (3), National Review (3), Daily Mail (3), Red State (3), Fox News (3), Shareblue (3), and PoliticusUSA (3), each with a value of 3. The "Other" category, shown in gray, has a value of 13. The segments are arranged in a circular pattern around the center, with labels and values clearly visible, and the chart includes a legend to identify each media source. The visual emphasis is on the relative size of each segment, with larger segments indicating higher citation frequencies.
